The provided leaf is specific to parvovirus B19 infection with vesiculobullous eruption on photo-exposed ears, which is not directly equivalent to polymorphous light eruption.

Juvenile spring eruption (JSE) is characterized by vesiculobullous lesions on photo-exposed areas, particularly the ears, and has been associated with parvovirus B19 infection. This aligns well with the vignette's description of a 13-year-old boy with intensely pruritic skin eruption, small blisters on both ears and vermillion border, and positive parvovirus B19 IgM/IgG antibodies and DNA in lesional skin. The leaf 'Acute parvovirus B19 infection with vesiculobullous eruption on photo-exposed ears' is clinically equivalent to this option.

The leaf 'Acute parvovirus B19 infection with vesiculobullous eruption on photo-exposed ears' is clinically equivalent to this option, as it describes the same condition.
